label: models/fw_console.mdl: a control console, waist high, dials, two screens, a row of switches

measured.lineup: ours is one of A to D in lineup.png beside models/hvr.mdl, models/big_rock.mdl, models/crystal.mdl: the judge does not know which

M1.reason: The outline is a waist-high box console with a slight top lip, which matches the brief's words. In the front and front-left views the console reads as a control desk, and no part sticks out or is missing.

M2.reason: Measured height is 37.5 against the asked 40, an offset of 6.3%, inside 15%. Length 62 and depth 26 are not given by the brief, so only the height can be checked against it.

M3.reason: The brief's parts are all present: two dark screens, three amber dials and a row of six red switches on the front. The dials are square blocks rather than round dials, so the shape is wrong for dials. Nothing else is asked for, and the sides and back are bare.

M4.reason: The regions read as what the brief calls for: grey painted, mottled steel body, dark green screen glass, amber dials and red switches. The colours are industrial and sit within Half-Life's palette.

M5.reason: Surface detail is thin. The front has no panel lines, labels, hazard stripe or wear beyond a faint edge highlight. The screens and dials carry no markings, so the surface reads as plain.

M6.reason: In the lineup it is clearly a manufactured object, but beside Half-Life's own props it reads as a plain box with simple blocky controls. A player would not take it for one of the game's props at game size.

M7.reason: The front with the screens and controls faces the viewer and is upright. The base sits flat and level in the below and side views, so it stands as a console would.

M8.reason: The SMAK check reports no errors. Triangles are 24, far under twice Half-Life's median of 105 and under the third quartile of 238. The below view shows a closed base, with no open or floating faces visible.
